subject: Pricing: Zenova mid-contract uplift, credit phasing and co-term question
messages:
From: Michelle Jiang <michelle.jiang@zenovahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Zenova Procurement <procurement@zenovahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-contract capacity top-up + invoice consolidation

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the Q2 check-in. We had an unexpected product usage bump last month and need to discuss adding capacity mid-contract (roughly ~60% uplift for the next 6 months) while keeping our renewal aligned with our fiscal year (co-term 2027-08-01). Our finance team prefers a single consolidated invoice and minimal separate line-items if possible.

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood provide a staged credit/bridge approach so we don't pay full uplift up-front?
- If we commit to the uplift, what discount bands apply to incremental usage and can the uplift be annualized/prorated to co-term at renewal?

Attaching our usage snapshot for the last 3 months.

[Attachment: current_usage_report.csv (CSV, 12 KB)]

Appreciate a quick outline of options so we can review before our procurement sync on Friday.

Best,
Michelle
Director, Analytics
Zenova Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michelle Jiang <michelle.jiang@zenovahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity top-up + invoice consolidation

Hi Michelle — thanks for the details and the usage file. Short answer: yes, we have a few standard patterns that customers use for mid-contract uplift while co-terming at renewal. I’ve looped in Marissa (pricing) and Aditya (solutions) to confirm sizing and invoicing mechanics.

Options we can outline quickly:
1) Staged bridge credit: Redwood issues a time-bound credit that covers the incremental uplift for N months; the customer pays the regular monthly invoice net of the credit. At renewal we can fold the uplift into an annualized commit and adjust the invoice cadence.
2) Incremental commit with discount ladder: Customer agrees to an uplift commitment for the remainder of the term; discounts apply only to incremental volume tiers. Discounts increase with larger top-ups or multi-quarter commitments.
3) Voucher/top-up model: Purchase prepaid vouchers that are redeemed against usage; better for single consolidated invoicing but requires up-front payment.

Question for Zenova: do you need the invoice to be a single line item at the GL level, or is a single monthly invoice with line breakdown acceptable? Also, when you say "annualize mid-term" — is the goal to have the uplift fully convert into an annual committed baseline on 2027-08-01?

We’ll prepare a short comparison (price impact, billing flow, accounting note) and send it back by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Priya
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Mid-contract capacity top-up + invoice consolidation

Priya / Aditya — following up with concrete pricing sketches for Michelle's ask. I attached a workbook with three scenarios; summary below.

[Attachment: pricing-models.xlsx (XLSX, 85 KB)]

Scenario A — Bridge Credit (preferred for accounting ease)
- 6-month bridge: Redwood issues a $XX,XXX credit applied monthly to offset incremental charges.
- At renewal (2027-08-01) we offer to fold 70% of the uplift into the new annual commit with a 10% discount on the folded portion.
- Invoicing: Single monthly invoice; credit shown as one line item (bridging credit).

Scenario B — Incremental Commit + Discount Ladder
- Customer commits to +60% incremental capacity for remainder of current term.
- Discount tiers on incremental usage: 0-30% = 7% off incremental unit price; 30-60% = 12%; >60% = 18%.
- Co-terming: We can annualize at renewal with an option to request a reconciliation credit if actual uplift differs by >15%.

Scenario C — Voucher / Prepay (finance prefers consolidated invoices)
- Purchase vouchers covering estimated uplift for 6 months; one invoice at purchase; vouchers redeemed monthly.
- Discount depends on prepay term: 6-month prepay = 8% discount; 12-month = 14%.

Notes / accounting considerations:
- We can produce a single consolidated invoice if Zenova requires a single GL line; billing will need a PO referencing the deal id.
- For annualization: we prefer folding a majority portion (50–75%) of uplift to prevent over-commit exposure; remainder can be left as on-demand.

I’ve flagged the draft amendment language (see redwood-draft-amendment.pdf) for Priya to share; it includes the credit mechanics and reconciliation window.

-Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Michelle Jiang <michelle.jiang@zenovahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Zenova Procurement <procurement@zenovahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity top-up + invoice consolidation

Thanks Priya / Marissa — helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement:

- Single GL line is preferable; can Redwood provide an invoice with one net amount that still allows us to see the sighted credit internally?
- We are open to Scenario A, but procurement prefers the bridge credit to be amortized across the 6 months (not a lump credit applied in month one).
- For the annualization path: Zenova would like the uplift to convert 100% to baseline at renewal if actual usage meets or exceeds uplift for 3 of the last 4 months before renewal. That is our preferred reconciliation rule.

Counter-proposal on economics: if Redwood will annualize 100% on that 3-of-4 rule, can you provide a 15% discount on incremental usage for the uplift portion (for the 6-month bridge window)? Procurement is flexible on voucher vs. bridge as long as invoice consolidation works.

We have a procurement review scheduled 2026-08-28 at 09:00 PT — would like to have a written option set to present.

Best,
Michelle
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michelle Jiang <michelle.jiang@zenovahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity top-up + invoice consolidation

Michelle — appreciate the clear counter-proposal and the procurement timeline. Per internal alignment here’s an offer we can present on Thursday: 

Offer (summary):
- Bridge amortization: Redwood will amortize a time-bound bridge credit across the 6-month uplift window (applied pro-rata to each monthly invoice). Invoicing: single monthly invoice (one net amount on GL) with an appended line for internal audit showing credit detail.
- Economics: 60% uplift for 6 months; incremental usage on uplift window receives a 15% discount (matches procurement ask).
- Annualization rule: If uplift usage >= committed uplift for 3 of the last 4 months before renewal, Redwood will fold 100% of the uplift into the annual baseline for the 2027-08-01 renewal. If not, we perform a reconciliation and issue a true-up credit or charge based on actuals (per workbook rules).
- Contract mechanics: sign a short amendment (I’ve attached the draft). We will require a PO referencing deal ZEN-2026-045 to enable single-line invoicing.

Next steps:
1) I’ll prepare a 1-page comparison (Scenario A as final with economics spelled out) and send to you by EOD tomorrow.
2) If procurement approves, we’ll route the amendment for signature and issue the PO details to Redwood Billing.

If you want Priya/Marissa/Aditya on the procurement call on 2026-08-28 at 09:00 PT, we can join.

Thanks — Priya
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
